references_named: Alan Turing, Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)
Roland Barthes, The Death of the Author (1967)
rationale: The mechanism genuinely enacts the argument: a regex stylometer scans its own rendered textContent, highlights the tells it was baited with, and returns a foregone verdict. Concept and execution are welded (P1), the AI detector is interrogated rather than merely used (P10), and the readymade logic is clean (P2). Double-coding works: surface gag is a detector catching itself; deeper layer is the death-of-the-author argument and the theatre of AI detection. Craft is restrained and the build is minimal (P3).
reservations: The novelty is real but the territory is crowded — Modernipsum and Artist's Statement already satirise language toys, and the 'AI detector as readymade' gesture, while sharp, leans on a 2023 discourse that may date quickly. The specimen text is deliberately seeded with tells, which makes the result feel rigged rather than discovered; a slightly more honest version might let the count actually drive the verdict (even if the verdict text is fixed).
revision_suggestion: Consider letting the confidence percentage be a function of the actual tell count with a wider spread (e.g. 60-99.9%) so the meter reads as a real measurement of the bait rather than a constant; this would sharpen the P1 claim that the mechanism is the argument.
